newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends lower in thin volume.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends lower in thin volume.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures ended modestly lower Monday in thin activity, pulled down by weaker CBOT grain and oilseed prices, traders said.
Cotton analysts also cited potential beneficial rains from the remnants of Tropical storm Danny across the U.S. southeast and rains which fell in dry cotton-growing areas of China.

Heavy rains Friday and Saturday will help ease a serious drought that has gripped much of northern China for the last few weeks, Chinese state media said on Sunday. The rains fell across Beijing as well as the provinces of Shaanxi, Shanxi, Henan and Hebei, the Xinhua news agency said.

The northern China plain has been extremely dry where they grow a lot of cotton, corn and soybeans, said Frank Schneider and Co cotton analyst Sharon Johnson. "This was the second rain event of the summer. This buys us some time for cotton. But it does not make a crop by any means," she said.
There were also potential beneficial rains from Tropical storm Danny. "We had a little bit of rain away from the Mobile (Ala.) area but it's very localized."

She believes that eventually next week "we should see some beneficial rain but it does not look as it will be very sizable." She added it was still dry in parts of the Delta where producers need rain.
Also, overseas export sales appeared to low, one analyst said.
December cotton closed down 0.35 cent at 74.58 cents a lb, with the rest 0.17 to 0.35 lower.
